evidence: Cic. Att. 16.2.1: ex tertiā pēnsiōne (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Our use: no reference work has a word for a subscription. Classically pēnsiō is a payment due at a set term, and the lexicon already pays by pēnsiōnēs (pay in instalments). A subscription is a pēnsiō mēnstrua or annua, paid for as long as one wants the thing.

Classically a signature or a line written underneath (Lewis & Short). Morgan–Owens warns that such words mean writing at the end of something, not subscribing; Traupman gives subscrībō among his computer terms.

sources: Lewis & Short: pensio · Lewis & Short: subscriptio
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. subscribe (to a periodical).
